title: Scammers use AI to impersonate immigration attorneys to dupe immigrants with fake legal services

reading.body:
AI tools were used to generate fake video and audio likenesses of a named, real attorney, then deployed at scale across social media platforms to advertise immigration services he does not offer. The failure mode is impersonation: synthetic media made a living person appear to say and do things he did not say or do, and that material was distributed through ordinary platform infrastructure with no mechanism in place to flag it as fraudulent before victims paid.

The fraud operated entirely outside the attorney's knowledge until clients began calling his office. Detection depended on the real person noticing something was wrong, not on any automated or platform-level check. By the time the scope became clear, thousands of fake profiles had already been active long enough to collect payments from victims, with one reported loss running into the thousands of dollars. Removal required the attorney to hire a private anti-piracy firm, and even then the process was reactive.

What is not established is who the scammers are, whether any law enforcement action has resulted in charges, or whether any platform was found to have violated its own policies in allowing the profiles to proliferate.

reports.title: Scammers steal identity of renowned Miami attorney to target immigrants on social media
South Florida immigration attorney says AI scammers are using his identity to target immigrants
Scammers use AI to impersonate immigration attorneys to dupe immigrants with fake legal services
Legal resident loses thousands seeking citizenship to AI immigration attorney

summary:
Angel Leal, a South Florida immigration attorney with more than 30 years of experience, has discovered that criminals are using artificial intelligence to impersonate him and defraud vulnerable immigrants. Scammers created hundreds of fake videos and social media profiles featuring AI-generated images of Leal offering immigration services he never provides. In one video, a digital version of Leal promises US residency assistance to undocumented immigrants for $2,200. Leal first learned of the scheme when potential clients began calling his office, though suspicious activity began last October and dramatically escalated over the past three months.

Leal's office hired an anti-piracy company that has successfully removed nearly 6,500 fake profiles across social media platforms, including 3,500 on TikTok, 2,400 on Facebook, and 544 on Instagram. The scams typically start with social media videos directing people to contact a WhatsApp number, where fraudsters send fake contracts and collect payment through apps like Venmo, Zelle, and Cash App. Leal has changed his personal phone number and plans to contact local and federal authorities to investigate. He warns immigrants to verify the identity of anyone offering legal services online and to be cautious of social media advertisements requesting immediate payment.
